entries.reason: Core owns the message buffer, so caller bytes are copied into native storage before the handle is returned.
Bytes is the explicit lifetime-independent snapshot API; the copy is required after the native message may close.
Message submit preserves the public caller handle with a binding-owned native staging copy; Core consumes the staged native part on ordinary synchronous rejection.
Core retains only a DONTWAIT wait token, context, and target, so the managed Send terminal must own an immutable logical packet that it can recreate after the matching WRITABLE record.
Each received native part needs a Go owner. The binding reuses wrappers when available and transfers the native message with zlink_msg_move without copying the payload.
Core writes topic metadata into caller-provided storage; the result objects retain one reusable buffer instead of allocating 64 KiB on every receive.
A builder supplied with []byte must materialize Core-owned messages before Submit returns.
Core writes option values into caller-provided scratch storage; returned strings and message values acquire Go ownership at the public boundary.

The binding joins submit results to completion records using the socket entry table, including WRITABLE records pulled before their entries are published. A caller driving Poller.Wait with PollCompletion registered drains the queue; asynchronous waiters on the result object do not drain it.
The package must link and load the runtime shipped beside the module, including in a clean consumer without repository paths.
